events.title: Frederick II regains Jerusalem by treaty
events.description: In the Sixth Crusade, Emperor Frederick II agreed a ten-year truce with the Ayyubid Sultan al-Kamil that returned Jerusalem to Christian control without a battle. The deal angered many on both sides.

events.title: Michelangelo dies in Rome
events.description: The sculptor, painter and architect died aged 88, still working as chief architect of St Peter's. His works include the David, the Sistine Chapel ceiling and the Last Judgement.
events.html: The sculptor, painter and architect died aged 88, still working as chief architect of St Peter's. His works include the David, the Sistine Chapel ceiling and the Last Judgement.

events.title: John Bunyan's 'The Pilgrim's Progress' is published
events.description: Partly written in Bedford gaol, Bunyan's allegory of Christian's journey to the Celestial City was an immediate success. It has been translated into more than 200 languages.
events.html: Partly written in Bedford gaol, Bunyan's allegory of Christian's journey to the Celestial City was an immediate success. It has been translated into more than 200 languages.

events.title: Mark Twain's 'Adventures of Huckleberry Finn' published in the US
events.description: Twain's novel of a boy and an escaped slave on the Mississippi was published in America. Written in vernacular speech, it has been called the source of all modern American literature.
events.html: Twain's novel of a boy and an escaped slave on the Mississippi was published in America. Written in vernacular speech, it has been called the source of all modern American literature.

events.title: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto
events.description: Comparing photographic plates at Lowell Observatory, Tombaugh found a faint moving object. Named Pluto at the suggestion of 11-year-old Venetia Burney, it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

events.title: Hans and Sophie Scholl arrested in Munich
events.description: The siblings of the White Rose resistance group were caught distributing anti-Nazi leaflets at Munich University. They were tried and guillotined four days later.
